title: Terraform UI Metadata
description: Schema for ui-metadata.json files that define how Terraform module variables are rendered as dynamic UI forms.

$schema.description: Reference to this JSON Schema for IDE validation.

module.description: Module identifier, matching the directory name (e.g., 'cloud-storage').

globals.description: Top-level Terraform variables that are NOT part of the repeatable resource object (e.g., project_id).

extras.description: Secondary/optional variable blocks beyond the primary resource (e.g., managed folder IAM bindings).

provides.description: What a resource built from this module can supply to another module's field. A field declares what it needs with data_source.resource; this declares what this module produces, so the platform can offer a resource that is being created in the same request as a value for a field that would otherwise only list what already exists in the cloud.

data_source.description: The data_source.resource identifier this module satisfies, e.g. compute.networks.

value_field.description: Which of this module's own fields holds the value a consumer needs. Must be a real field id, and is usually the key_field.

satellites.description: Resources this module creates besides the primary one, which have no independent lifecycle and are therefore not separate catalog modules (MODULE_CONTRACT R4). Declaring them lets the UI warn that they are not adopted on import.

deprecated.description: If true, this module is hidden from the new-request picker but still fully rendered and editable for resources that already use it. Set when a replacement module id supersedes this one (MODULE_CONTRACT R9).

deprecation_note.description: Why this module is deprecated and what replaces it. Shown wherever the module still appears. Only meaningful when `deprecated` is true.

display.description: How the module appears in the resource catalog UI.

icon.description: Icon identifier used by the frontend (e.g., 'cloud-storage', 'compute-engine').

description.description: Short description shown in the catalog card.

resource.description: Describes the primary repeatable resource variable — typically a map(object({...})).

key_field.description: Which field inside the object serves as the map key / resource identifier (e.g., 'app_name').

key_label.description: Human-readable label for the key field (e.g., 'Bucket name').

key_description.description: Help text for the key field.

locked_after_create.description: If true, the resource key cannot be changed while editing an existing managed resource.

sections.description: Groups of related fields, rendered as collapsible sections.

label.description: Section heading shown in the UI.

collapsed.description: If true, the section starts collapsed. Default: false.

description.description: Help text / tooltip shown under the field.

required.description: Whether the field is mandatory. Default: inferred from Terraform optional().

default.description: Pre-filled default value. Type should match the field type.

nullable.description: If true, the field can be set to null (renders as a 'None' / 'Disable' option). Default: false.

locked_after_create.description: If true, this field is read-only while editing an existing managed resource.

multiline.description: Render a text field as a multi-line editor rather than a single-line input. For values that are genuinely documents — startup scripts, cloud-init, embedded config. Only meaningful on type "text"; the stored value is an ordinary string either way.

ui_only.description: If true, this control does not map to a Terraform attribute or global; it only parameterises another field's data_source (e.g., artifact-registry's remote_password_secret). Exempts the field from the CI check that every control maps to an object attribute or a global (MODULE_CONTRACT R6).

sensitive.description: The value is a secret in its own right, not a reference to one. Marks a field whose value must not be logged, and whose presence makes an exported archive secret-bearing. Do not set it for a field naming a Secret Manager secret or version — those carry no secret material.

import.description: Declares how an existing cloud resource is adopted into this module. Omit it and the module is create-only.

module.description: Label of the `module` block in main.tf this import targets. Defaults to resource.variable, which is not always right (cloud-run declares module "cloud_run_v2" for variable cloud_run). Set it explicitly whenever they differ.

target.description: Resource address INSIDE the wrapped remote module, e.g. 'google_storage_bucket.bucket'. Must not include the 'module.<label>["<key>"]' prefix, which Sela Craft adds.

id_template.description: The provider's documented import ID format, with {field_id} placeholders resolved from identity_fields.

identity_fields.description: Field ids needed to build id_template uniquely. Must include resource.key_field. project_id may appear here even though it is injected from the environment rather than entered by the user.

field_map.description: Resource attribute name -> ui-metadata field id, for every field whose names differ. Identically-named fields need no entry.

ignore.description: Attributes with no live counterpart, so they can never cause a false mismatch (e.g., force_destroy).

requires_review.description: Forces human review of this module's imports regardless of the generic flow. Set it for anything sensitive.

targets.description: For modules owning several addresses. The first entry is the primary — its attributes supply the tfvars key. Use this instead of `target`/`id_template`.

satellite.description: A secondary resource created by this module that has no independent lifecycle (MODULE_CONTRACT R4).

address.description: Terraform address of the satellite inside the wrapped remote module, e.g. 'google_storage_bucket_iam_member.members'.

driven_by.description: The ui-metadata field id whose value creates these resources, e.g. 'iam_members'. Omit when the module always creates the satellite.

note.description: Plain-language consequence shown to the user, e.g. 'IAM bindings are not adopted on import; existing bindings stay unmanaged.'

value.description: The actual value sent to Terraform.

pattern.description: Regex pattern the value must match.

pattern_error.description: Custom error message when the pattern doesn't match.

depends_on.description: Conditional visibility — show this field only when another field meets a condition.

field.description: The id of the field this depends on.

value.description: The value the dependency field must have for this field to be visible.

data_source.description: Dynamic data source — fetch options from backend at runtime instead of using static options.

params.description: Query parameters to send. Each key is a param name, value is a source definition.

display.description: How to map response items to dropdown options.

value_key.description: Response field to use as option value.

label_key.description: Response field to use as option label.

description_key.description: Response field to use as option description.

allow_custom.description: Allow freeform text entry in addition to fetched options. Default: false.

cache_ttl.description: Cache the response for this many seconds. Default: 300.

param_source.description: Source of a query parameter value — either read from another form field or a static constant.

from_field.description: Read value from another form field's current value.

extra.description: A secondary Terraform variable, typically a map(object({...})).

import_target.description: One Terraform address a single tfvars entry owns. Modules that own a set of resources declare several; a VPN is a gateway plus forwarding rules plus a tunnel.

id.description: Stable identifier for this target within the module.

target.description: Resource address inside the wrapped remote module.

id_template.description: The provider's documented import ID format for this resource type.

index.description: Index suffix when the resource is count/for_each indexed inside the module, e.g. "[0]".

required.description: When false, a target that does not exist is skipped rather than failing the import. The cloud is the authority on existence, which avoids re-implementing the module's own conditional logic here.

field_map.description: Resource attribute path -> field id, for this target's contribution.
